transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah… I guess I’m here because of elevators. I know that probably sounds kind of silly, and I know they’re not actually dangerous, but when I have to get in one I get really scared—like I’m going to get trapped in there. I just can’t seem to make myself feel normal about it.
Do you avoid other situations or places besides elevators because of similar fears?

Um… no, not really that I can think of. It’s mostly just elevators. I mean, I might feel a little uneasy in some tight places, but I don’t really avoid anything else on purpose. At least, I don’t think so.
Do you ever feel afraid or panicky in places or situations where you feel escape might be difficult, like being in a crowd, on a bridge, or in a closed-in space?

I mean… mostly it’s elevators. I don’t really get that way in crowds or on bridges, not that I’ve noticed. It’s just when I have to get in an elevator, even though I know it’s not really dangerous, I get scared I’m going to be trapped in there. I know that probably sounds dramatic, but that’s the thing I can’t seem to make feel normal.
Have you ever had a panic attack in situations like being outside the home alone, in open spaces, or in public transportation, even if you weren't in an elevator?

Um… I don’t think so, no. Not that I can remember. I mean, I can get nervous about the elevator thing, but outside by myself or open spaces… that doesn’t really happen to me. Public transportation isn’t really the same for me either, as far as I’ve noticed. Does that answer it okay?
When you’re not near an elevator, does this fear still bother you? Like, do you worry about getting into an elevator even when you’re not in one or planning to use one?

Not usually, no… I mean, it’s not like I’m sitting at home worrying about elevators all day. It’s more when I know I have to get in one, or I’m right there by one, then it kind of hits me. I know they’re not really dangerous, but I start feeling like I could get trapped and I can’t really talk myself into feeling normal about it. Does that make sense?
Have you ever had a panic attack specifically while in an elevator?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d call it a full panic attack, but it feels pretty close sometimes. As soon as the doors start sliding shut, my chest gets tight, my hands get sweaty, and I just think, “I need to get out,” even if it’s only a few floors. I know that probably sounds silly, but that’s what happens.
Have you ever had a panic attack in situations that weren’t related to elevators, like in open spaces, on a bus or train, or when you were alone outside your home?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, buses or being outside alone don’t really do that to me. It’s more tied to the elevator situation. I haven’t noticed panic like that in other places, at least not that I can remember. Is that what you’re asking?
Have you ever felt sudden, intense fear or panic in open spaces, like a park or a large field, even if you weren’t near an elevator or a tight space?

No, I don’t think so. Like, parks or big open areas don’t really scare me that way. If anything, I’m usually fine there. It’s not something I’ve noticed happening away from elevators or places like that… I hope that answers it right.
Have you ever felt sudden fear or panic in other enclosed spaces, like a small room, a car, or a subway train, even if you weren’t in an elevator?

Not really, no. I mean, a small room or a car doesn’t usually set me off like that. Subway trains… I don’t ride them much, but I can’t think of a time I panicked there. It seems more like the elevator thing for me, if that makes sense.
Have you ever felt sudden, intense fear or panic when you’re away from elevators—like when you’re leaving your home alone, in a crowd, or on a bridge?

No, I don’t think so. Leaving home by myself or being in a crowd doesn’t usually make me panic like that. Bridges either, not that I can remember. It really seems more connected to elevators for me… if that makes sense.
